issues.text: The paper deviates from the pre-analysis plan by treating second-generation child health outcomes as secondary outcomes subordinate to a fertility analysis, and by including infant mortality although the PAP listed only under-5 mortality. The evaluator says these deviations are not acknowledged or explained in the manuscript.
issues.quote: Second generation child health outcomes were pre-registered as "secondary" outcomes related to a primary analysis of participants' fertility rather than focal outcomes themselves.

issues.text: The pre-specified child health index, which is the first child health outcome listed in the PAP, does not appear in the paper, and the evaluator sees no explanation for its omission.
issues.quote: But, this child health index does not appear in the paper.

issues.text: The PAP's secondary hypothesis test using an F test on the joint significance of the original deworming treatment and the cost-sharing treatment is absent from the paper.
issues.quote: The PAP proposes a secondary hypothesis test that uses an F test to examine the joint significance of the original de-worming treatment and the cost-sharing treatment but I did not see this in the paper.

issues.text: The PAP states the authors will report multiple-hypothesis-adjusted p-values, but the manuscript does not include them.
issues.quote: In addition, the PAP states that the authors will report multiple hypothesis adjusted p-values, but the manuscript does not contain them.

issues.text: The paper lacks formal first-stage statistics showing how much more likely treated-group children were to receive deworming and how many additional years of medication they actually received. Without these, the magnitude of the reduced-form effects cannot be properly interpreted.
issues.quote:
The authors do not present formal statistics on the "first
stage"

issues.text: The reported average of 2.41 additional years of exposure likely overstates actual treatment given roughly 75% take-up and treatment reaching the control group, so the effective dose difference is probably smaller (perhaps 1.7 to 1.8 years). The difference in the likelihood of any deworming during adolescence may also be small between groups.
issues.quote: The paper states that group 1 and group 2 schools received "on average" 2.41 additional years of exposure to the PSDP, but take-up was about 75%, with some amount of treatment reaching the control group.

issues.text: The analysis does not show whether baseline characteristics differ between survey respondents and non-respondents by treatment arm. Such a check is needed to assess whether residual attrition could bias results, even though attrition is low.
issues.quote: One additional helpful piece of information would be to show differences in baseline characteristics across respondents and non-respondents by treatment arm.

issues.text: Marriage quality is mentioned only in a footnote as a future-research mechanism, yet the evaluator argues it is relevant to this paper. Because both mother's and father's health appear equally important, the untreated spouse's health could be the actual mechanism, for example through assortative matching.
issues.quote:
this seems like a relevant
outcome to consider for this paper.

issues.text: The evaluator notes some residual uncertainty in the main result because not all sampled participants completed the follow-up surveys.
issues.quote:
some uncertainty may
remain due to the fact that not all sampled participants completed the follow-up surveys.
